title: Capacity heuristics and sentinel playtest — week notes
content:
Context: quick capture from the weekly infra sync focused on the sentinel autoscaling playtest and capacity heuristics experiment. This is intentionally a lightweight, informal note for handoff to oncall and next week's planning.

Date / meeting: 2028-09-19, 09:30 PT, infra sync (30m)
Facilitator: Priya
Attendees: Priya, Evan, Lena, Marcus, Samir (+ async from ops team)

One-line summary:
We finished the third run of sentinel autoscaling against an APAC-edge surge profile. Observed faster cold-start reduction after adding a short priming step for RPC kernels, but saw a 6% increase in token-cost under heavy prefix-cache churn. Decision: keep priming enabled for regions with >75% short-session traffic; extend Canary to dedicated pools next week.

Key observations (raw):
- Sentinel playtest run 3 (09:00–09:20): simulated 4x baseline QPS from Sydney edge for 20m. Autoscaler scaled to target sooner than v2 (median scale time 45s -> 31s).
- Priming microstep: we pushed a lightweight kernel-touch before routing; latency p95 improved by ~120ms during first 30s of burst.
- Cache churn: dominant cost seen when concurrent unique contexts > cache capacity. Eviction noise increased KV misses -> 6% token cost increase on that run vs control.
- Fallbacks: model-variant fallback triggered correctly on node preemption in eu-west-1 simulation; some sessions experienced format-change warnings in logs (tracked in INFRA-3982).
- Disk-backed KV warmers: experimental warmer reduced cold-run token spend by 9% but added ~30MB/sec network IO during ramp — need to evaluate on smaller nodes.

Metrics snapshots (important numbers):
- Median scale latency (baseline v2): 45s; sentinel v3: 31s
- P95 generation latency during ramp (with priming): 1.08s -> without priming: 1.20s
- Token cost delta (cache churn scenario): +6%
- Cold-start token spend reduced (warmer enabled): -9%
- Network IO spike when warmer runs: +30MB/s per node for 20–40s

Action items (owner / due):
1) Marcus: create a trimmed config for priming to use in Dedicated pools (limit network IO) — due 2028-09-24.
2) Evan: schedule a focused canary for dedicated-west region and add monitoring thresholds for token-cost drift — due 2028-09-22.
3) Samir: write a short runbook addendum for ops covering: when to disable priming, how to roll back warmer, and emergency thresholds — due 2028-09-21.
4) Priya + Lena: run a controlled experiment on cache sizing heuristics (vary eviction target and measure token-cost) — start 2028-09-25, results by 2028-10-02.
5) All: annotate INFRA-3982 with example session traces for the fallback-format warnings (helpful for runtime team) — ongoing.

Open questions / tradeoffs to track:
- Priming benefit vs IO overhead: for APAC edge the latency wins look compelling, but the network IO may push underutilized nodes past NIC limits in certain clouds. Need a cost/benefit threshold.
- Autoscaler aggressiveness: shorter scale latency helps p99 and user-facing latency but increases churn and potential thrash. Should we clip scale-down aggressiveness for the first 60s after a burst?
- Cache eviction policy: LRU tuned for long sessions is hurting short-session workloads. Consider hybrid LRU + frequency bias for short-session pools.

Notes-to-self / informal thoughts (scratchpad):
- If we can detect "short-session heavy" traffic earlier (heuristic: median request tokens < 48 over last 60s) we can flip to small-cache profile and enable priming. Implement as routing metadata so decisions are lightweight.
- Could we do an adaptive priming length: short burst -> single-touch priming; sustained burst -> fuller kernel warm. Avoid network spike for tiny ramps.

Risks and mitigations observed:
- Risk: Warmer causes transient network congestion on hosts sharing ENI -> mitigate by rate-limiting warmer connections (Marcus exploring connection pooling).
- Risk: Canary in Dedicated may surface capacity accounting edge cases with reserved allocations -> Evan to confirm billing view aligns with expected metrics.

Communication / handoff notes:
- Ops: Samir to post a short summary to #infra-ops with the run's key numbers and the action items to disable priming if network IO > configured threshold.
- Runtime: open PR for a safer fallback-message handling (see linked PR) and ask runtime team to review sample traces.

Next steps for next week:
- Run dedicated-west canary, with priming limited config, observe token-cost and network IO. (Evan)
- Begin cache-sizing AB test (Priya+Lena).
- Convert key findings into a short one-pager for Eng Leads if we want to push priming as default for APAC-edge.

Appendix (useful links and refs):
- Playtest orchestration job: github.com/redwood-inference/playbooks/jobs/runner/523
- JIRA ticket for fallback warnings: JIRA-INFRA-3982
- Draft design note for priming: confluence/capacity-heuristics-ux
- Runtime PR (fallback handling): github.com/redwood-inference/runtimectl/pull/421

End of notes.

Quick state: draft — will refine before posting to the weekly infra digest.
